title: Adversaries and what holds against each.
caption: Trusted, not adversaries: the Soroban host and validators, the verifier contracts documents name, the adopted recovery controller, the wallet's display of what is signed, and, for the proofs, the Lean kernel, Charon, Aeneas and the specification. T-labels refer to the statements in {{ref:sec:proofs}}.
rows: A1 Grantee (app or agent key)
Sign within rules that name its key; build any invocation tree; cite any rule that names its key

An accepted authorization is allowed by the rules it cites (proved, T2). No grant rule allows a call to the account, its adopted recovery controller, or the ZK adapter and pool of its recovery configuration (proved, T8–T9; runtime recheck tested). Each capped rule's window stays within its limit from installation (proved, T6)
A key named by several live rules has the union of their authority. Caps are per rule, not per grant. Allowances, and funds held by other contracts, move without the account's authorization
A2 Submitter or relayer
Wrap signed entries, choose timing and fee, resubmit a refused entry until its expiration ledger
An external signer's signature binds this account and the selected rule IDs (tested; a paper proof in the formal appendix of the academic edition)
Delegated signers do not bind rule IDs. A rule edited in place between signing and inclusion decides under its new contents
A3 Thief of the owner key
Everything the owner can do
Under Protected, once the recovery condition authorizes an attempt, the account authorizes only its completion; changing recovery or upgrading needs the condition's evidence (tested)
Under Loss the thief can cancel any recovery. Allowances survive recovery. An owner upgrade executes after {{fact:upgrade-delay-ledgers}} ledgers
A4 Guardians below quorum
Approve attempts
Completion needs the quorum, the delay and the window (tested)
A full quorum is trusted
A5 Manager or admin of `perch/verifiers`
Admit verifier names; the admin can upgrade the registry
An applied account, and its pinned infrastructure addresses, are unaffected by later registry actions
Names resolved by later installs follow the manager. One key holds both roles on testnet and mainnet
